'''Brenda Muriel Lansdown''' (January 25, 1904 – July 1, 1990) was an English-born American math and science educator and a professor of education at [[Brooklyn College]]. Her method for teaching science became popular in China after she lectured at [[Beijing Normal University]] in the 1980s.

==Early life and education==
Lansdown was born in London, the daughter of George Arthur Lansdown and Muriel Janet Lansdown. Her father was an architect who served on the [[Metropolitan Borough of Kensington|Kensington Borough Council]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1946-12-20 |title=The Death of Ald. G. A. Lansdown; Fine Record of Public Work |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-kensington-news-and-west-london-time/194875778/ |access-date=2026-04-04 |work=The Kensington News and West London Times |pages=1 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She graduated from [[University of Lausanne|Lausanne University]],<ref name=":0" /> and moved to the United States in 1931.<ref>Lansdown's middle name, birthdate, and emigration date are from her petition for naturalization, dated April 25, 1935, via Ancestry.</ref> She earned a bachelor's degree from [[Hunter College]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=1958-01-16 |title=Educator Talks in Spring Valley on Sputnik Age |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-journal-news-educator-talks-in-sprin/194897422/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |work=The Journal News |pages=6 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
==Career==
Lansdown taught at New York City private schools in the 1940s, including the [[Dalton School]] and the [[City and Country School]]. She was known for her hands-on science lessons, which she called the investigation-colloquium method. She taught education courses at Brooklyn College,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1952-03-14 |title=Community School Conference Set |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/brooklyn-eagle-community-school-conferen/194901233/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |work=Brooklyn Eagle |pages=26 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Hunter College, and the [[Harvard Graduate School of Education]].<ref name=":0" />

Lansdown was interested in both educational technology and preparing students for a more technologically complex future. In 1958, she spoke about science education in the "Sputnik Age".<ref name=":1" /> In 1963, she coordinated a project to develop best practices for effective and engaging videotaped instruction.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1963-06-22 |title='Idiot Box' is Put to Good Use by BC Education Department |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/kings-courier-idiot-box-is-put-to-good/194897140/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |work=Kings Courier |pages=2 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She traveled to China in 1977 to study science education.<ref name=":12">{{Cite journal |last=Lansdown |first=Brenda |date=November–December 1979 |title=Sharing Science in the Classroom: An Alternative Teaching Method |url=https://archive.scienceforthepeople.org/vol-11/v11n6/sharing-science-in-the-classroom-an-alternative-teaching-method/ |journal=Science for the People |volume=11 |issue=6 |pages=22–25}}</ref> In 1984, with [[UNICEF]] funding, she returned to China to give workshops on her science teaching method, and spoke at Beijing Normal University.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Fowler |first=Glenn |date=1990-07-04 |title=Brenda Lansdown, Who Devised a Way To Teach, Dies at 86 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/07/04/obituaries/brenda-lansdown-who-devised-a-way-to-teach-dies-at-86.html |access-date=2026-04-04 |work=The New York Times |page=13|language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Eddy|first=David |title=A US educator whose work is venerated in China |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1986/0501/dben-f1.html |access-date=2026-04-04 |work=Christian Science Monitor |issn=0882-7729}}</ref>
==Publications==
Lansdown's academic research was published in scholarly journals including ''[[American Journal of Education|The School Review]],''<ref name=":2" /> ''[[Science Education (journal)|Science Education]],''<ref name=":3" /> ''Childhood Education,''<ref name=":4" /> ''[[The Reading Teacher]],''<ref name=":5" /> ''The Arithmetic Teacher,''<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /> ''[[Pi Lambda Theta|Educational Horizons]],''<ref name=":9" /> ''[[National Science Teaching Association|Science and Children]],''<ref name=":10" /> and ''[[Teachers College Record]].''<ref name=":11" />

==Personal life==
Lansdown died in 1990, at the age of 86, in Boston.<ref name=":0" />
